title: Threshold Orchestrator for Cohort-aware Eviction Sentinels
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a threshold orchestration service that generates automated rollback triggers (eviction signals) for model rollouts. The system will fuse multiple SLO signals — P95 latency, error rate, token cost per request, and throughput/backpressure — and generate cohort-specific thresholds and confidence envelopes. The orchestrator should account for traffic cohorts (region, customer tier, model input length distributions) and apply temporal smoothing to avoid noisy flip-flopping. Primary outputs: safe abort decision, graded eviction score, suggested traffic ramp-back percentage, and human-readable justification for Console UI and on-call alerts.
design_notes: Use cohort baselining: compute per-cohort historical distributions over the last 14 days and bootstrap confidence intervals for each metric.
Signal fusion strategy: weighted z-score fusion with per-signal sensitivity knobs and optional Bayesian change-point detection for abrupt regressions.
Cost-normalized triggers: normalize token cost signal against baseline cost-per-token for the model variant to avoid false positives when model outputs lengthen legitimately.
Decision hysteresis: require sustained breach for 3 contiguous 1-min windows or a single high-severity breach above emergency multiplier before auto-eviction.
Safety fallbacks: automatic downgrade path prefers cheaper but compatible model variant; full traffic evacuation requires 2x severity and cross-signal agreement.
Observability hooks: expose per-cohort score time series and rationale via rollout-logs and Console dashboard.
Privacy: cohort identifiers must be hashed at ingress and stored in ephemeral buffers to avoid PII in metrics datasets.
tasks: Prototype cohort baseline computation job (Go) and storage schema in timeseries DB
Implement signal fusion library with pluggable aggregators (zscore, bayes, quantile)
Integrate cost-normalization function with billing metrics for token cost per request
Add API endpoints for 'eviction-score' and 'eviction-decision' with traces and rationale
Console: small UI card to surface cohort-level eviction scores and 'why' text
E2E tests: synthetic canary run harness and failure injection scenarios
Create runbook for on-call and escalation thresholds
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator emits eviction-score and decision events for every staged rollout request path
System demonstrates >85% precision and >75% recall on a labeled synthetic regression dataset for latency and error modes
Console surfaces cohort-level rationale and a button to pause auto-eviction during investigation
Safe rollback path exercised in a dry-run canary (no customer-facing traffic impact) and reviewed by SRE
Latency overhead introduced by orchestrator in critical path <5ms p50 and <15ms p95
test_plan: Generate synthetic cohorts (region, tenant tier, short/long inputs) and replay historical metrics with injected regressions
Run chaos scenarios: upstream DB lag, missing billing metrics, and transient spike noise to ensure hysteresis prevents flapping
A/B test: enable orchestration for internal-only canary traffic, compare operator interventions vs. baseline for 2 weeks
Load test: ensure orchestrator scales to 1k concurrent canaries without queueing delays
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flag behind 'evict-orch' default off, run in shadow mode for 2 weeks
Phase 1: enable auto-evaluation mode with no auto-eviction; send alerts to SRE/PM for 1 week
Phase 2: limited auto-eviction for non-critical customers (10% of traffic) with manual override available
Phase 3: full rollout guarded by canary policy after 2 successful weeks and a tabletop review
metrics: p95 latency delta (candidate vs baseline) per cohort
5-min rolling error rate and burst factor
token cost per request normalized by baseline length
eviction-score distribution and true positive / false positive rate on labeled corpus
operator override rate and mean time to investigate after an eviction
